Title: Mary Gitau is Becoming the Nurse She Always Dreamed Of
NewsSummary: SONAM student aims to serve underserved communities with compassion
NewsContent:
Mary Gitau's journey to becoming a nurse began on a quiet Saturday when an email brought a lifelong dream within her grasp. The acceptance letter to Aga Khan University's School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa (SONAM EA) was more than just an offer; it was the first step toward a career where she could make a tangible difference.

Walking onto the AKU campus as a new undergraduate nursing student, Mary was immediately struck by the welcoming atmosphere. The professional staff and calm environment reinforced her choice to pursue a path of personal growth and professional excellence. Orientation week solidified this feeling, as she met her classmates, the largest group she had ever studied with, and was inspired by their shared goals and a strong sense of teamwork.

Faculty interactions left a lasting impression, particularly one powerful piece of advice: "In nursing, there are no second chances; every action we take is irreversible." This lesson became a guiding principle for her. It underscored the importance of not just technical skills, but also the right attitude, a crucial element for interacting with patients and providing compassionate care.

Stepping into the science lab was another turning point. Its modern, spacious design and advanced equipment showed her how AKU connects theory to practice, building confidence and preparing students for the real-world demands of healthcare.

Mary chose nursing because she believes it's both a science and a calling. She envisions a future serving underserved communities, educating people, and providing not just treatment, but also compassion and emotional support. Her early weeks at AKU have been eye-opening, broadening her perspective beyond the classroom and reminding her of the need for resilience in the face of challenges.

Like other AKU students who are finding a path that transforms their dreams into reality, Mary isn't just training to be a nurse; she's preparing to become a voice of hope and a source of holistic care for every patient she encounters. The years ahead will not only equip her with professional skills but also shape her into the empathetic, courageous nurse she always hoped to be. At SONAM EA, she is finding the knowledge and support to turn her aspirations into a lasting legacy of care.
